description: Add, modify or delete sudo rule within IPA server using IPA API.

parameters.name: cmd
parameters.description: List of commands assigned to the rule. If an empty list is passed all commands are removed from the rule. If option is omitted commands are not checked nor changed.

parameters.name: cmdcategory
parameters.description: Command category the rule applies to. Choices: "all"

parameters.name: cmdgroup
parameters.description: List of command groups assigned to the rule. If an empty list is passed all command groups are removed from the rule. If option is omitted command groups are not checked nor changed.

parameters.name: cn
parameters.description: Canonical name. Can not be changed as it is the unique identifier.

parameters.name: deny_cmd
parameters.description: List of denied commands assigned to the rule. If an empty list is passed all commands are removed from the rule. If option is omitted commands are not checked nor changed.

parameters.name: deny_cmdgroup
parameters.description: List of denied command groups assigned to the rule. If an empty list is passed all command groups are removed from the rule. If option is omitted command groups are not checked nor changed.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Description of the sudo rule.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: List of hosts assigned to the rule. If an empty list is passed all hosts are removed from the rule. If option is omitted hosts are not checked nor changed. Option hostcategory must be omitted to assign hosts.

parameters.name: hostcategory
parameters.description: Host category the rule applies to. If all is passed one must omit host and hostgroup. Option host and hostgroup must be omitted to assign all. Choices: "all"

parameters.name: hostgroup
parameters.description: List of host groups assigned to the rule. If an empty list is passed all host groups are removed from the rule. If option is omitted host groups are not checked nor changed. Option hostcategory must be omitted to assign host groups.

parameters.name: ipa_host
parameters.description: IP or hostname of IPA server. If the value is not specified in the task, the value of environment variable IPA_HOST is used instead. If both the environment variable IPA_HOST and the value are not specified in the task, then DNS is used to try to discover the FreeIPA server. The relevant entry needed in FreeIPA is the ipa-ca entry. If neither the DNS entry, nor the environment IPA_HOST, nor the value are available in the task, then the default value is used. Default: "ipa.example.com"

parameters.name: ipa_pass
parameters.description: Password of administrative user. If the value is not specified in the task, the value of environment variable IPA_PASS is used instead. Note that if the urllib_gssapi library is available, it is possible to use GSSAPI to authenticate to FreeIPA. If the environment variable KRB5CCNAME is available, the module uses this Kerberos credentials cache to authenticate to the FreeIPA server. If the environment variable KRB5_CLIENT_KTNAME is available, and KRB5CCNAME is not; the module uses this Kerberos keytab to authenticate. If GSSAPI is not available, the usage of ipa_pass is required.

parameters.name: ipa_port
parameters.description: Port of FreeIPA / IPA server. If the value is not specified in the task, the value of environment variable IPA_PORT is used instead. If both the environment variable IPA_PORT and the value are not specified in the task, then default value is set. Default: 443

parameters.name: ipa_prot
parameters.description: Protocol used by IPA server. If the value is not specified in the task, the value of environment variable IPA_PROT is used instead. If both the environment variable IPA_PROT and the value are not specified in the task, then default value is set. Choices: "http" "https" ← (default)

parameters.name: ipa_timeout
parameters.description: Specifies idle timeout (in seconds) for the connection. For bulk operations, you may want to increase this in order to avoid timeout from IPA server. If the value is not specified in the task, the value of environment variable IPA_TIMEOUT is used instead. If both the environment variable IPA_TIMEOUT and the value are not specified in the task, then default value is set. Default: 10

parameters.name: ipa_user
parameters.description: Administrative account used on IPA server. If the value is not specified in the task, the value of environment variable IPA_USER is used instead. If both the environment variable IPA_USER and the value are not specified in the task, then default value is set. Default: "admin"

parameters.name: runasextusers
parameters.description: List of external RunAs users.

parameters.name: runasgroupcategory
parameters.description: RunAs Group category the rule applies to. Choices: "all"

parameters.name: runasusercategory
parameters.description: RunAs User category the rule applies to. Choices: "all"

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: State to ensure. Choices: "absent" "disabled" "enabled" "present" ← (default)

parameters.name: sudoopt
parameters.description: List of options to add to the sudo rule.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: List of users assigned to the rule. If an empty list is passed all users are removed from the rule. If option is omitted users are not checked nor changed.

parameters.name: usercategory
parameters.description: User category the rule applies to. Choices: "all"

parameters.name: usergroup
parameters.description: List of user groups assigned to the rule. If an empty list is passed all user groups are removed from the rule. If option is omitted user groups are not checked nor changed.

parameters.name: validate_certs
parameters.description: This only applies if ipa_prot is https. If set to false, the SSL certificates are not validated. This should only set to false used on personally controlled sites using self-signed certificates. Choices: false true ← (default)

examples:
- name: Ensure sudo rule is present that's allows all every body to execute any command on any host without being asked
    for a password.
  community.general.ipa_sudorule:
    name: sudo_all_nopasswd
    cmdcategory: all
    description: Allow to run every command with sudo without password
    hostcategory: all
    sudoopt:
      - '!authenticate'
    usercategory: all
    ipa_host: ipa.example.com
    ipa_user: admin
    ipa_pass: topsecret

- name: Ensure user group developers can run every command on host group db-server as well as on host db01.example.com.
  community.general.ipa_sudorule:
    name: sudo_dev_dbserver
    description: Allow developers to run every command with sudo on all database server
    cmdcategory: all
    host:
      - db01.example.com
    hostgroup:
      - db-server
    sudoopt:
      - '!authenticate'
    usergroup:
      - developers
    ipa_host: ipa.example.com
    ipa_user: admin
    ipa_pass: topsecret

- name: Ensure user group operations can run any commands that is part of operations-cmdgroup on any host as user root.
  community.general.ipa_sudorule:
    name: sudo_operations_all
    description: Allow operators to run any commands that is part of operations-cmdgroup on any host as user root.
    cmdgroup:
      - operations-cmdgroup
    hostcategory: all
    runasextusers:
      - root
    sudoopt:
      - '!authenticate'
    usergroup:
      - operators
    ipa_host: ipa.example.com
    ipa_user: admin
    ipa_pass: topsecret

return_values.name: sudorule
return_values.description: Sudorule as returned by IPA. Returned: always
